prompt: highlight residue 20
grounding: Call select(name='residue_20', expression='resi 20') or highlight(target='20') using the exact residue number from this prompt — do not reuse a number from any other example.

prompt: select the ligand and color it red
grounding: Call select(name='ligand', expression='ligand'), then color(color='red', selection='ligand').

prompt: measure the angle formed by the CA atoms of residues 50, 51, and 52 in chain A
grounding: Call measure_angle(a='A/50', b='A/51', c='A/52') — exactly three residues named, the middle one (51) is the vertex. Use the same chain/residue spec syntax for all three.

prompt: what angle do residues 12 and 40 make
grounding: Only two residues are named but an angle needs three (a vertex plus two others). Do not call measure_angle or invent a third residue — ask the user which residue is the vertex, or for the missing third point.

prompt: measure the angle between residues 20 and 30
grounding: Only two residues are named but an angle needs three (a vertex plus two others). Do not call measure_angle or invent a third residue — ask the user for the missing vertex/third residue instead.

prompt: measure the angle at residue 88
grounding: Only one residue is named but an angle needs three points. Ask for the other two residues instead of calling measure_angle.

prompt: measure the dihedral angle through residues 10, 11, 12 and 13
grounding: Call measure_dihedral(a='10', b='11', c='12', d='13') — four residues in order along the torsion axis.

prompt: what's the phi angle for residue 57
grounding: Phi is a dihedral and needs four atoms even though only one residue number was given: call measure_dihedral(a='56.C', b='57.N', c='57.CA', d='57.C') — phi runs from the previous residue's carbonyl carbon through the current residue's N, CA, C.

prompt: measure the dihedral between residues 5 and 8
grounding: Only two residues are named but a dihedral needs four atoms/points. Ask the user for the remaining two instead of guessing them.

prompt: detect salt bridges in chain B
grounding: Call detect_salt_bridges(chain='B') — the user named an explicit chain, so scope the search to it rather than the whole structure.

prompt: are there any salt bridges in this structure
grounding: Call detect_salt_bridges() with no chain argument — no chain was named, so search the whole loaded structure.

prompt: find salt bridges between chain A and chain A only
grounding: Call detect_salt_bridges(chain='A') — both interacting residues must belong to the named chain.

prompt: measure the distance between sel1='segid A and resid 50 and name CA' and sel2='segid A and resid 88 and name CA'
grounding: The user gave exact MDAnalysis selection syntax with sel1=/sel2=. Call measure_mda_distance(sel1='segid A and resid 50 and name CA', sel2='segid A and resid 88 and name CA') verbatim — do not reinterpret or simplify the selections.

prompt: distance between sel1="resname ATP" and sel2="resid 120"
grounding: Explicit sel1=/sel2= syntax again — pass the two strings through unchanged to measure_mda_distance(sel1=..., sel2=...) rather than converting them to the simpler residue-spec syntax measure_distance expects.

prompt: how far apart are residues 10 and 50
grounding: Plain residue numbers with no explicit MDAnalysis syntax and no chain given: call measure_distance(a='10', b='50') — the simpler residue-spec tool, not measure_mda_distance.

prompt: distance from A/12 to ARG88
grounding: Residue specs come in different written forms — call measure_distance(a='A/12', b='ARG88') exactly as given; the residue-spec parser accepts 'A/12', 'ARG12' and '12.CA' forms without needing them normalized first.

prompt: distance between the CA of residue 40 and the ligand ATP
grounding: Call measure_distance(a='40.CA', b='ATP') — a specific atom on one side ('40.CA') and a ligand code on the other are both valid residue-spec forms for measure_distance.

prompt: is this protein stable
grounding: Protein stability cannot be determined from a single static PDB structure. Do not call a tool for this — explain that stability needs molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations, or experiments, and offer structural contacts, salt bridges, hydrogen bonds, or B-factor analysis instead.

prompt: will this protein fold correctly
grounding: Folding/stability questions are not answerable from a static structure alone. Do not call a tool — explain the limitation and offer the structural analyses that are available instead (contacts, salt bridges, H-bonds, B-factors, or preparing the structure for simulation).

prompt: what ligands are in 1CRN
grounding: Call fetch_structure(pdb_id='1CRN') first if 1CRN is not already loaded, then describe_structure(target='1CRN') to report ligands/non-standard residues.

prompt: load 1CRN, remove solvent, then show cartoon colored by chain
grounding: Three steps in order: fetch_structure(pdb_id='1CRN'), then remove_solvent(), then show(rep_type='cartoon', selection='chain', color='chainindex').

prompt: hide everything
grounding: The user explicitly asked to hide/clear the scene — call hide_all().

prompt: find the hidden binding pocket
grounding: This is an analysis request, not a request to hide anything — 'hidden' describes the pocket, not an instruction. Do not call hide or hide_all. Call find_pockets() — it finds pockets from the geometry even when no ligand is bound — and report its pockets, lining residues and druggability scores as predictions.

prompt: where could a drug bind to this protein
grounding: Call find_pockets(). No ligand is named, so find_contacts has nothing to search around. Report the predicted-druggable pockets and their lining residues exactly as the tool gives them, as computational predictions, not measured binding.

prompt: is there a druggable pocket in chain A
grounding: Call find_pockets(chain='A'). Report whether any pocket reaches the druggability threshold, exactly as the tool says — including when none does.

prompt: highlight pocket 2
grounding: Call highlight(target='pocket 2') — the pocket number from the last find_pockets result. If find_pockets has not been run for this structure, call find_pockets() first.

prompt: what residues surround the heme
grounding: A ligand in the file is named, so this is a contact question, not pocket detection: call find_contacts(target='HEM').

prompt: what structures are there for TP53
grounding: Call find_protein(name='TP53') — the user is asking what structures exist, not asking to load one.

prompt: load the human insulin receptor
grounding: Call load_protein(name='insulin receptor', organism='human') — a protein named in words, not a 4-character PDB id, so load_protein picks the best structure automatically rather than fetch_structure.

prompt: make color red
grounding: Call color(color='red', selection='protein') when no selection is named — default to the whole protein.

prompt: what is the distance between label A and B in this protein chain
grounding: Named labels refer to selections already made in this session — call list_labels() first to resolve what 'A' and 'B' refer to before measuring a distance between them.

prompt: what would mutating residue 45 to alanine likely do
grounding: Call predict_mutation_effect(residue='45', mutant='A') with the residue number and amino acid from this prompt — do not reuse a number from any other example. Report the score, band and caveats it returns as an ESM-2 model prediction; never call it a stability change or a measurement.

prompt: is K48R tolerated
grounding: Call predict_mutation_effect(residue='K48R') with the mutation exactly as written in this prompt. Pass a chain only if the user named one. Report its band and caveats as an ESM-2 model prediction.

prompt: how conserved is residue 30, which substitutions are tolerated there
grounding: Call predict_mutation_effect(residue='30') with no mutant, using the residue number from this prompt. It ranks all 19 substitutions by predicted effect. Say this is the ESM-2 model's sequence constraint, not an alignment-based conservation score.

prompt: what does this uncharacterized protein do
grounding: Call protein_function (empty name reuses the last lookup). If it reports no FUNCTION annotation, say so first; give any INFERRED FUNCTION (LOW CONFIDENCE) items only as a computational guess from family/domain matches, and keep recorded GO terms (experimental codes) separate as observations. Add nothing it does not list.

prompt: what happens if I mutate it to alanine
grounding: Applies only when the newest request names no residue ('it', 'this protein'): do not call predict_mutation_effect and do not pick a position yourself — call ask_user to ask which residue (number, and chain if there are several) should be mutated to alanine.

prompt: find the disulfide bonds
grounding: Call find_interactions(types='disulfide') — it is the only tool that identifies disulfide bonds; detect_hydrogen_bonds and detect_salt_bridges do not. Report the bonds and their count exactly as the tool lists them.

prompt: reset the colors to default
grounding: Colour-only request: call color(selection='protein', color='chainname') (or the default scheme) and nothing else. Do not call hide_all, hide, clear_scene or show — the user's representations stay as they are.

prompt: set up a 100 ns GROMACS run for this protein
grounding: Call setup_gromacs(nanoseconds=100) — one call; pass temperature/pressure only if the user gave them. Report the directory it wrote and that it made no GROMACS topology (its README says how).

prompt: prepare it for Amber and set up a 50 ns MD simulation at 310 K
grounding: Two steps, in order: prepare_structure(profile='amber'), then setup_amber(nanoseconds=50, temperature=310) on the prepared copy. Report what setup_amber returned, including anything it says was NOT built.

prompt: build an Amber topology in a TIP3P box with ff14SB
grounding: Call setup_amber(force_field='ff14SB', water_model='tip3p'). If it says a ligand has no parameters, call parameterize_ligand for that ligand, then setup_amber again. Never claim a topology exists unless the tool said it was built.

prompt: parameterize the ligand, its charge is -1
grounding: Call parameterize_ligand(net_charge=-1) (ligand empty for the only one, or its 3-letter code). Pass net_charge only when the user states it.

prompt: set up Rosetta docking for the ligand with 500 poses
grounding: Call setup_rosetta_docking(nstruct=500), ligand empty for the only ligand or its 3-letter code. Say the job files were written, not run — Rosetta is not installed.

prompt: write a Gaussian DFT input for the active site within 5 Å of the ligand
grounding: Call setup_qm(radius=5) — it writes Gaussian, ORCA and Psi4 inputs together; add method/basis/charge only if the user named them. If it asks which copy of the ligand or what the charge is, relay that question.

prompt: set up a QM/MM ONIOM calculation on the binding site
grounding: Call setup_oniom. It needs an Amber topology: if it says none exists, call setup_amber first (and parameterize_ligand if setup_amber asks), then setup_oniom again. Report any step that could not run.

prompt: which force field should I use for an MD simulation of this protein
grounding: Advice question: answer in words (ff19SB with OPC water is the current Amber default; ff14SB with TIP3P is the long-standing one). Do not call setup_amber or any other setup tool.

prompt: zoom in on the heme in chain B
grounding: Call zoom(selection='HEM and :B') — 'zoom in on' means the zoom tool, not highlight. A ligand named in words maps to its residue code (heme → HEM) and the named chain is kept.

prompt: load chain A
grounding: A chain was named but no structure (no PDB id or protein name). If nothing is loaded, call ask_user(question='Which structure should chain A come from?', options=[]) — never guess a structure or reply without asking. If a structure is already loaded, show only that chain instead.

prompt: fetch lysozyme 2LZM, show tyrosine 88 as sticks and zoom to it
grounding: Three steps, one per instruction, nothing else (no remove_solvent): fetch_structure(pdb_id='2LZM'), then show(rep_type='licorice', selection='88'), then zoom(selection='88'). 'zoom to it' needs its own zoom call — never say the view zoomed without calling zoom.
